products.name: CoCounsel (Casetext)
products.note: Legal research AI; litigation support; Westlaw integration; attorney work product risk

reading.body:
Thomson Reuters built a legal AI product by acquiring Casetext and integrating it with its existing Westlaw platform, positioning AI as a tool that extends attorney capacity rather than replacing it.

CoCounsel operates within Thomson Reuters's existing ecosystem of legal content and research tools. The company frames this as "Fiduciary-Grade AI," emphasizing that the product works from established legal databases and research materials rather than operating as a standalone model. This matters because legal work carries direct liability risk. By anchoring CoCounsel to Westlaw and Practical Law content, Thomson Reuters addresses the core problem: attorneys need tools that reduce work hours without introducing novel legal reasoning that could create malpractice exposure. The reported case of a firm doubling litigation capacity suggests the value proposition is labor efficiency, not new legal capability.

Thomson Reuters developed an in-house language model called Thomson in August 2026, signaling a shift toward owning the compute layer rather than relying entirely on third-party models. Whether this model powers CoCounsel or other products, or serves as a future direction, is not specified in the available data. The company's annual research reports on AI adoption across legal, tax, and accounting sectors suggest it is also tracking market demand and professional concerns, though the specific findings are not detailed here.

The data does not cover Thomson Reuters's infrastructure investments, energy consumption, or whether it hosts models on its own servers or relies on cloud providers. It also does not address how CoCounsel's performance compares to other legal AI products, pricing, or adoption rates beyond the single Greenberg Traurig case.

profile_text.body:
Thomson Reuters is a publicly traded global content and technology company headquartered in Toronto, listed on both the Nasdaq and TSX under the ticker TRI, with a CIK of 0001075124. The company describes itself as delivering purpose-built technology to empower professionals in legal, tax, trade, and risk fields to make faster decisions and gain sharper insights. Its platform offerings span legal research and drafting, trade compliance automation, and integrated tax and risk management through a connected suite it calls ONESOURCE+.

The company's primary AI product is CoCounsel, described as built on principles the company terms "Fiduciary-Grade AI" and integrated with its Westlaw and Practical Law content. CoCounsel is positioned for legal professionals handling litigation support, research, and drafting workflows, and the company notes it is launching production-grade agentic workflows on the platform capable of handling multi-step tasks. Global law firm Greenberg Traurig, LLP is cited as having deployed the next generation of CoCounsel Legal. A case study on the site describes a firm called Justly Prudent using CoCounsel and Westlaw AI and reporting a 100% increase in litigation capacity. In August 2026, Thomson Reuters also announced the launch of Thomson, described as the company's first proprietary large language model developed in-house.

The held facts record CoCounsel, acquired through Casetext, as Thomson Reuters' tracked AI product in the Finance and Legal AI category, with noted considerations around attorney work product risk. No litigation or MCP server entries are present in the held facts.
